headings.35: B. There Was No Breach of Procedural Fairness

blocks.overview: The case concerns a 60-year-old Jamaican citizen (Applicant) seeking judicial review of a refusal of her second permanent residence application on humanitarian and compassionate (H&C) grounds by Canada (Respondent). The Applicant challenged the reasonableness of the Officer's decision and alleged procedural fairness breaches. The Federal Court dismissed the application, finding the Officer's decision reasonable and no procedural fairness breach.

blocks.issue: Was the Officer's decision reasonable regarding the weight given to the Applicant's establishment in Canada, including unauthorized work and stay?
blocks.court_conclusion: Officer reasonably assigned negative weight to unauthorized work and stay; decision was justified and reasonable.

positions.text: Officer improperly diminished establishment weight due to unauthorized work and stay, penalizing unauthorized work contradicts H&C purpose.
Officer properly assigned negative weight to unauthorized work and stay; balanced commendation with noting unauthorized work weighs against applicants.
H&C exemptions are discretionary; no rigid formula; relief justified if reasonable person would desire to relieve misfortunes.

blocks.issue: Did the Officer err in assessing the Applicant's evidence of front-line work and employment, including reliance on a sworn affidavit?
blocks.court_conclusion: Officer did not make a credibility finding but found insufficient objective evidence; decision entitled to deference.

positions.text: Affidavit has high probative value; no further evidence required; Officer erred by requiring more and made veiled credibility finding.
Rejects presumption of truthfulness without sufficient evidence; Officer found insufficient objective evidence, not credibility finding; decision explained and reasonable.
Officer found little objective evidence beyond affidavit; assigned little weight to employment evidence; noted financial support deficiencies.

blocks.issue: Was there a breach of procedural fairness by the Officer, including failure to hold an oral interview or making a veiled credibility finding?
blocks.court_conclusion: No breach of procedural fairness; no right to interview in H&C context; no credibility finding made.

positions.text: Officer breached procedural fairness by veiled credibility finding without oral interview.
No right or expectation of interview; Officer made no credibility finding; no procedural fairness breach.

propositions.text: Applicant is a 60-year-old Jamaican citizen seeking judicial review of a negative decision dated April 30, 2021 refusing her second permanent residence application under H&C grounds.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the Applicant is a 60-year-old Jamaican citizen seeking judicial review of a negative H&C permanent residence decision dated April 30, 2021.

propositions.text: Applicant entered Canada in March 2012 and overstayed temporary resident status before refugee claim refusal on September 5, 2017.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the Applicant entered Canada in 2012, overstayed, and had a refugee claim refused in 2017.

propositions.text: Applicant's first H&C application refused June 21, 2018; PRRA refused January 25, 2019; warrant issued April 17, 2019 after failure to appear for removal.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the Applicant's first H&C and PRRA applications were refused and a warrant was issued after she failed to appear for removal.

propositions.text: Applicant filed second H&C application on September 2, 2020, arguing her front-line work, establishment, financial support to family, education, connections, hardships if returned, and grandchildren's interests.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant argues in her second H&C application that her work, establishment, family support, education, connections, hardships, and grandchildren's interests justify relief.

propositions.text: Officer found Applicant had small positive establishment, insufficient hardship evidence, and returning was in grandchildren's best interest; denied exemption under IRPA section 25(1).

paragraphs.summary: The Officer found limited establishment, insufficient hardship, and that return was in grandchildren's best interest, denying H&C exemption.

propositions.text: Applicant asserts Officer erred by mitigating establishment weight due to unauthorized stay/work, undervaluing affidavit on front-line work, misassessing country conditions, and breaching procedural fairness by veiled credibility finding without oral interview.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant alleges errors in the Officer's assessment of establishment, affidavit evidence, country conditions, and procedural fairness breach.

propositions.text: Application for judicial review shall be dismissed.

paragraphs.summary: The court concludes the judicial review application will be dismissed.

propositions.text: Issues: whether Officer's decision was reasonable and whether procedural fairness was breached.

paragraphs.summary: The court identifies issues as reasonableness of the Officer's decision and procedural fairness breach.

propositions.text: Presumptive standard of review is reasonableness; no exceptions apply per Vavilov.
Reasonableness requires decision to be transparent, intelligible, justified, with coherent rationale and justified outcome per Vavilov.
Court intervenes only if serious shortcomings undermine justification, intelligibility, transparency.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the reasonableness standard applies, requiring transparent, justified decisions, intervening only for serious shortcomings.

propositions.text: Procedural fairness review involves no deference; fairness judged by substantive rights and consequences.
Ultimate question is whether Applicant knew case to meet and had full, fair chance to respond.

paragraphs.summary: The court states procedural fairness review is non-deferential, focusing on whether Applicant had fair opportunity to respond.

propositions.text: Section 25(1) IRPA allows Minister discretion to grant permanent residence on H&C grounds by weighing all relevant considerations cumulatively.
Relief justified if reasonable person would desire to relieve misfortunes, per Kanthasamy and Caleb cases.

paragraphs.summary: The court explains section 25(1) IRPA grants discretionary H&C relief if reasonable person would desire to relieve misfortunes, citing cases.

propositions.text: H&C exemptions are exceptional, discretionary, deserving considerable deference per Qureshi.
No rigid formula determines outcome per Sivalingam.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes H&C exemptions are exceptional, discretionary, and no rigid formula applies, citing Qureshi and Sivalingam.

propositions.text: Applicant argues Officer improperly diminished establishment weight due to unauthorized work and stay, citing Baeza case.
Applicant contends penalizing unauthorized work contradicts H&C program purpose.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant argues the Officer wrongly diminished establishment weight for unauthorized work and stay, citing Baeza and program purpose.

propositions.text: Applicant asserts Officer relied on irrelevant factors (unauthorized work and stay) in assigning negative weight to establishment, rendering decision unreasonable.
Applicant asserts Officer failed to address submissions that work without authorization cannot be penalized, violating Vavilov's justification requirement.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant alleges the Officer relied on irrelevant factors and failed to justify penalizing unauthorized work, breaching Vavilov.

propositions.text: Rozgonyi decision addressed similar argument and held on issue of unauthorized work and establishment weight.

paragraphs.summary: The court cites Rozgonyi decision addressing similar argument on unauthorized work and establishment weight.

propositions.text: Court agrees with Rozgonyi and finds Officer properly assigned negative weight to unauthorized work and stay in balancing exercise.

paragraphs.summary: The court agrees with Rozgonyi and finds Officer properly assigned negative weight to unauthorized work and stay.

propositions.text: Officer carefully considered evidence and submissions on establishment factors and reasonably found small positive establishment.
Court will not reassess or reweigh establishment if Officer's assessment is not unreasonable.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds Officer reasonably balanced establishment factors and will not reweigh them.

propositions.text: Applicant asserts her front-line personal support worker role during COVID-19 should weigh heavily in favour of granting application.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant asserts her front-line work during COVID-19 should weigh heavily in her favour.

propositions.text: Applicant submitted sworn affidavit attesting to employment history and inability to obtain employer documentation due to unauthorized work.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant submitted a sworn affidavit about her employment history and inability to get employer documents due to unauthorized work.

propositions.text: Officer found little objective evidence beyond Applicant's affidavit to prove personal support worker employment or health-care sector work and assigned little weight to this factor.

paragraphs.summary: The Officer found insufficient objective evidence of Applicant's personal support worker employment and assigned little weight to it.

propositions.text: Officer failed to understand legal implications of Applicant's sworn affidavit statements
Applicant's affidavit has high probative value due to sworn truth and perjury penalty
No further objective evidence required for Officer to accept affidavit
Officer erred by requiring further evidence and not explaining insufficiency of affidavit

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues Officer misunderstood affidavit's legal weight, erred by requiring more evidence and not explaining insufficiency.

propositions.text: Officer did not believe Applicant's evidence and made a veiled credibility determination

paragraphs.summary: Applicant alleges Officer disbelieved her evidence, making a veiled credibility finding.

propositions.text: Rejects Applicant's assertions about presumption of truthfulness of sworn statements
Applicant cannot rely on sworn statement truthfulness without sufficient supporting evidence
Cites Lin and Barros Barros cases supporting need for sufficient evidence
Officer's disbelief not assumed when evidence insufficient to meet legal burden on balance of probabilities
Cites Ferguson and Gao cases on burden of proof and evidence sufficiency

paragraphs.summary: Court rejects Applicant's claims, explains sworn statements need supporting evidence and insufficient evidence doesn't imply disbelief.

propositions.text: Officer made no credibility finding but found insufficient objective evidence of employment
Officers get deference on sufficiency findings if explained and not disguised credibility findings
Cites Magonza case on deference and explanation of evidentiary insufficiency
Officer adequately explained evidence deficiencies and what was missing

paragraphs.summary: Court finds Officer did not make credibility finding but reasonably found insufficient evidence with adequate explanation.

propositions.text: Lack of sufficient evidence on employment was one of many deficiencies noted by Officer
Officer noted little objective evidence of employment and financial situation from 2012-2017
No evidence supporting employment at Better Home Care or caregiver job
Unclear how Applicant supported herself since arriving in Canada
Applicant submitted insufficient evidence to show financial stability or independence

paragraphs.summary: Officer found many evidentiary deficiencies including insufficient proof of employment and financial stability.

propositions.text: Applicant submitted family letters indicating financial support while in Jamaica
Letters unclear about financial support after Applicant came to Canada
Applicant submitted one money transfer receipt from April 2020
Applicant provided some support but insufficient evidence that family primarily relied on her
Applicant's uncertain financial status undermines claim as main financial supporter

paragraphs.summary: Officer found insufficient evidence that Applicant was main financial supporter of family given uncertain finances.

propositions.text: Applicant has 17 grandchildren in Jamaica, but little info on most of them
One grandchild is 24 years old, another two children aged 13 and 2
Applicant's youngest grandson has heart condition but no objective medical evidence provided
Some grandchildren may be BIOC age and benefited from Applicant's support
Insufficient evidence family primarily relied on Applicant financially or that loss of income would greatly affect grandchildren
One granddaughter employed, indicating not reliant on Applicant's support

paragraphs.summary: Officer found insufficient evidence that grandchildren primarily relied on Applicant financially or would be greatly affected by income loss.

propositions.text: Counsel's claim that Applicant and family would fall into poverty without Canadian income is baseless
Some children were unemployed at one point but no evidence all currently unemployed

paragraphs.summary: Officer found no evidence that Applicant's family would fall into poverty without her Canadian income.

propositions.text: Family criticizes Officer's reference to unauthorized work as negative factor
Cites Fidel Baeza case where steady employment without permits should not be held against applicants

paragraphs.summary: Applicant criticizes Officer's negative view of unauthorized work, citing Fidel Baeza case.

propositions.text: Subsection 25(1) presupposes IRPA non-compliance but provides relief
Cites Mitchell case on subsection 25(1) purpose
Evidence of establishment may be considered in light of circumstances including illegality
Cites Aguilar Sarmiento, Semana, Damian cases on considering illegal work
Officer reasonably balanced commendation of efforts with noting unauthorized work weighs against applicants

paragraphs.summary: Court finds Officer reasonably balanced positive factors with negative weight of unauthorized work.

propositions.text: Applicant says Officer failed to address her role as front-line worker during COVID-19
Applicant's submissions emphasized multiple factors, not just COVID-19 work
Officer expressly addressed Applicant's COVID-19 work submission

paragraphs.summary: Applicant claims Officer ignored COVID-19 work; court finds submissions included many factors and Officer addressed COVID-19 work.

propositions.text: Officer's findings on hardship finding work in Jamaica are inconsistent and unintelligible
Officer found Applicant may face hardship but education and experience improve employment prospects

paragraphs.summary: Applicant alleges inconsistent hardship findings; court finds Officer's decision consistent and reasonable.

propositions.text: Officer failed to consider risk of discrimination and sexual harassment in Jamaica
Risk was part of submissions on employment difficulties and was expressly addressed by Officer

paragraphs.summary: Applicant alleges Officer ignored risk of discrimination; court finds it was addressed as part of employment hardship.

propositions.text: New arguments at hearing not in Applicant's memorandum are improper and will not be entertained

paragraphs.summary: Court will not entertain new hearing arguments not raised in Applicant's memorandum.

propositions.text: Officer made adverse credibility finding disguised as insufficiency, requiring oral interview

paragraphs.summary: Applicant alleges Officer made disguised credibility finding requiring oral interview.

propositions.text: No right or expectation of interview in H&C context
Exceptions exist when decision clearly based on credibility finding
Cites Owusu, Duka, Shpati cases on interview rights and credibility findings
Officer made no credibility finding, only sufficiency determination
No breach of procedural fairness by not holding oral interview

paragraphs.summary: Court finds no credibility finding, no interview right, and no procedural fairness breach by Officer.

propositions.text: Applicant failed to show Officer's decision unreasonable or procedural fairness breach
Application for judicial review dismissed

paragraphs.summary: Court dismisses judicial review as Applicant failed to show unreasonableness or procedural fairness breach.

propositions.text: No question for certification arises

paragraphs.summary: Court agrees no question for certification arises.
